title: Module 3 quiz — Spring Boot Engineering
description: Eight questions on IoC, REST idempotency, ProblemDetail, JPA transactions, Actuator probes, and BayPay tests. All names and amounts are synthetic.

questions.prompt: PaymentController takes PaymentApplicationService in its constructor. A teammate wants to replace that with ApplicationContext.getBean(PaymentApplicationService.class) inside create. Why refuse?
choices: Spring cannot inject controllers that have constructors
A service locator hides the dependency graph, blocks simple fakes, and lets create grow invisible collaborators
Constructor injection is deprecated in Spring Boot 3.5
getBean is slower than field @Autowired on the repository
questions.explanation: IoC is useful when dependencies are declared. A locator hides them and forces a context to unit-test the adapter. Constructor injection is the BayPay default, not a deprecated API.

questions.prompt: Avery Chen’s merchant app retries POST /api/v1/payments with the same Idempotency-Key and the same 25.00 USD body after a timeout. What must BayPay return, and what must not happen?
choices: 201 and a new paymentId; the ledger should show two PAYMENT rows
200 and the original paymentId; the ledger must not gain a second PAYMENT row
409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT because all retries are conflicts
204 with an empty body so clients do not store duplicates
questions.explanation: Identical key and canonical hash is a replay: 200 and the original resource. A second 201 or a second ledger post is a double charge. 409 is for the same key with a different body.

questions.prompt: CreatePaymentRequest amount 0 fails Bean Validation. A completed payment over-refund fails in RefundApplicationService. Which HTTP pair is correct?
choices: Both 400 VALIDATION_FAILED because all money rules are syntax
Amount 0 is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED; over-refund is 422 REFUND_EXCEEDS_REMAINING
Both 422 because ProblemDetail cannot represent 400
Amount 0 is 500; over-refund is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT
questions.explanation: Jakarta Bean Validation on the record is syntactic (400). Remaining-amount is a domain rule after load (422 with a BayPay code). Collapsing them loses client and WAF signal.

questions.prompt: ApiExceptionHandler’s catch-all Exception handler must do which pair?
choices: Return the exception message in the 500 body and skip logging to avoid PII
Log the stack with the request URI (correlation id is already in MDC) and return a generic 500 detail
Translate every Exception to 422 so payments never look like outages
Rethrow so Tomcat can render an HTML error page
questions.explanation: Operators need the stack in logs. Clients and attackers must not receive SQL or class names. 422 is for domain validation, not bugs. HTML error pages break the ProblemDetail contract.

questions.prompt: PaymentApplicationService.create is @Transactional. PaymentPostingService.postAuthorized is not. A RuntimeException escapes during ledger save. What happens to the AUTHORIZED payment row?
choices: It commits; only the ledger rolls back because posting lacks @Transactional
The whole create transaction rolls back, so the payment is not left AUTHORIZED/COMPLETED without a ledger post
Spring commits because posting is in another Maven module
H2 ignores rollback; PostgreSQL would roll back
questions.explanation: Posting joins the caller’s transaction. A propagating RuntimeException rolls back every table in that unit of work. Maven module boundaries are not transaction boundaries. H2 and PostgreSQL both honor the TM.

questions.prompt: A @Transactional refund method catches Exception around the ledger insert, logs, and returns a successful CreateResult. Why can finance miss the ledger row while GET /refunds/{id} returns COMPLETED?
choices: open-in-view is false, so ledger entities never flush
The exception never leaves the proxy, Spring commits the refund, and the HTTP adapter maps the result to 201
STRING enums cannot represent REFUND ledger types on H2
Idempotency-Key forces read-only transactions
questions.explanation: Default rollback requires a RuntimeException to propagate. Swallowing it commits flushed work (the refund). That is the FIX-304 class of defect. OSIV and enum mappings are unrelated.

questions.prompt: PostgreSQL is unreachable for 30 seconds in prod. Which Actuator policy should BayPay use?
choices: Liveness DOWN so Kubernetes restarts the JVM every few seconds until the database returns
Readiness DOWN (stop traffic) and liveness UP if the process is otherwise healthy
Expose /actuator/heapdump so on-call can see stuck threads
Disable probes and let the load balancer TCP-ping port 8080
questions.explanation: A DB blip is a readiness failure, not a reason to kill the JVM. Heapdump on the payment port is a data leak. TCP checks cannot see a wedged dispatcher or a down DataSource.

questions.prompt: Which test strategy actually proves BayPay’s payment write contract?
choices: @WebMvcTest that mocks PaymentApplicationService and asserts the controller returns 201
@SpringBootTest + MockMvc (PaymentApiIT) covering 201, replay 200, 409, 422, and missing-key 400 against H2
A unit test that verifies PaymentRepository.save was called once
Manual curl on local only, because Testcontainers is required for every assertion
questions.explanation: The money contract is HTTP + validation + idempotency + JPA. PaymentApiIT boots the composition root. Mocking the service or the repository does not prove replay. Testcontainers is optional fidelity, not a substitute for the H2 IT matrix.
